title: LPG Subsidy Reform, Energy Compensation, and Social Risk in Bolivia: A Machine-Learning Agent-Based Microsimulation
abstract: arXiv:2609.00414v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This study evaluates alternative designs for reforming Bolivia's liquefied petroleum gas subsidy using a machine-learning agent-based microsimulation framework. The analysis harmonizes household survey data, expenditure data, demographic and health information, and monthly hydrocarbon production and commercialization series to simulate fiscal savings, poverty effects, energy substitution, administrative costs, and social risks under multiple reform scenarios. The model compares uncompensated subsidy removal, fixed energy transfers, full compensation for vulnerable LPG users, voucher-based compensation, maternal-child transfers, clean-energy transition kits, and hybrid policy packages. Machine-learning models are used to learn household vulnerability, fuel-use patterns, food insecurity risk, and behavioral propensities that feed into a monthly agent-based simulation. translated_title: 玻利维亚的液化石油气补贴改革、能源补偿与社会风险：一种机器学习基于主体的微观模拟
translated_abstract: 本研究采用机器学习与基于主体建模相结合的微观模拟框架，评估了玻利维亚液化石油气补贴改革的多种替代设计方案。该分析整合了住户调查数据、支出数据、人口与健康信息以及月度碳氢化合物生产与销售序列，以在多种改革情景下模拟财政节约、贫困效应、能源替代、行政成本和社会风险。该模型比较了无补偿的补贴取消、固定能源转移支付、对脆弱液化石油气用户的完全补偿、基于券的补偿、母婴转移支付、清洁能源转型套装以及混合政策方案。机器学习模型被用于学习住户脆弱性、燃料使用模式、粮食不安全风险和行为倾向，并将这些结果输入到月度基于主体的模拟中。结果显示，在无补偿的情况下取消补贴会产生……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文创新性地将机器学习与基于主体的微观模拟相结合，评估玻利维亚液化石油气补贴改革的多种设计方案在财政节约、贫困影响、能源替代和社会风险方面的表现。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a novel machine-learning agent-based microsimulation framework to evaluate alternative LPG subsidy reform designs in Bolivia, comparing their fiscal savings, poverty effects, energy substitution, and social risks across multiple policy scenarios.
